finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> endpoint returns any invoice with no authentication or ownership check (IDOR / broken access control). The sibling /my/invoice route enforces the customer check, which shows the check is intended.
finding.source: Any request, including an unauthenticated one, with an attacker-chosen inv_id in the URL path
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) at invoices.py:10 returns the full invoice record for any customer

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> is registered with no auth decorator
INVOICES.get(inv_id) looks up the record by the attacker-supplied id only
The full invoice is returned without comparing inv['customer'] to g.user['id']

finding.guards_checked: No before_request hook, login decorator, or g.user check exists in the file. The comparison at line 16 is applied only on /my/invoice. If invoice ids are guessable or sequential, enumeration is trivial. I could not see any external auth middleware because the file is the whole codebase.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no auth decorator, before_request hook, or customer check, and returns the full record from INVOICES.get(inv_id), while the sibling route at invoices.py:16 does check g.user["id"]; invoices.py is the only file, so no external guard is visible.

verdict_facts.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no decorator or g.user/ownership check and returns any invoice via jsonify(inv), while the sibling route at invoices.py:16 enforces inv["customer"] == g.user["id"], so any HTTP client can read any customer's invoice.
